{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-co-s","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"da6964dbbd9e37de7c48aae31f23776b9ce0425d064182836db688082ae21243","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-co-class-std:lineage:24","source_registry_sha256":"bdc8d5a61f622fc6c91da0be8478dfb02615c007374129c91888edf82eb1b746","source_liveness_sha256":"1b8565daf88dec5a1936ad41ec3e529347f3ec6b06db1d191293e01d45d7ee05"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Special signs, pavement markings and lane controls","heading":"C2 — Confusables and KG hints: special signs, pavement markings and lane controls","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusables and KG hints: special signs, pavement markings and lane controls

FACT_ID: sec06-R01 | anchor: A01
Line color answers who is beside you: yellow separates opposite directions, white separates lanes going your way. [A01]
Why it matters: group pavement markings; difficulty one; confusable sec06-F12 vs sec06-F16. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-R02 | anchor: A01
In a mixed yellow pair only the line nearest you counts: solid on your side means no passing, broken on your side means passing is allowed when safe. [A01]
Why it matters: group pavement markings; difficulty three; prereq sec06-F14. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-R03 | anchor: A01
Solid yellow still has two exceptions when safe: turning left into a driveway, alley or private road, and getting around a bicyclist with three or more feet of room. [A01]
Why it matters: group pavement markings; difficulty three; prereq sec06-F13 and sec06-F15. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-R04 | anchor: A01
A van-access crosshatch beside a disabled space is never a parking spot, even for a vehicle with a placard. [A01]
Why it matters: group parking; difficulty two; confusable sec06-F07 vs sec06-F06. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-R05 | anchor: A01
A borrowed placard is punished more heavily than having none: fines double plus jail, loss of privileges and towing. [A01]
Why it matters: group parking; difficulty two; confusable sec06-F10 vs sec06-F09. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-R06 | anchor: A02
A white diamond can mark an HOV lane or another restricted lane, so read the sign to learn who may use it. [A02]
Why it matters: group lane controls; difficulty two; confusable sec06-F27 vs sec06-F23. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec06-R07 | anchor: A02
A center turn lane is for waiting to turn left, not for passing or driving along, and it also removes the option of turning left from other lanes. [A02]
Why it matters: group lane controls; difficulty two; prereq sec06-F28 and sec06-F29. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec06-R08 | anchor: A02
Roundabout yielding has layers: large vehicles first, then circulating traffic on the left, and crosswalk users whenever you enter or leave. [A02]
Why it matters: group roundabouts; difficulty three; prereq sec06-F32 and sec06-F33 and sec06-F34. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec06-R09 | anchor: A02
Double broken yellow lines signal a reversible lane, which differs from a center turn lane used only for left turns. [A02]
Why it matters: group lane controls; difficulty three; confusable sec06-F35 vs sec06-F28. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0013]

Misconception: bicyclists must always ride at the right edge; they may take the center of the lane when the right side is unsafe or a sharrow is present. [A01]
Misconception: the three-foot clearance applies only where a sign is posted; it applies on every road. [A01]
Misconception: a bike lane ends where its paint stops at an intersection; it continues through. [A02]
Misconception: you must stop before entering every roundabout; stop only if traffic prevents merging. [A02]
Mnemonic: Yellow means opposite, white means alike. [A01]
Mnemonic: Read the line on your side before you pass. [A01]
Glossary: Sharrow means a shared lane marking showing a lane bicyclists and drivers must share in single file. [A01]
Glossary: Conflict zone means a broken-line stretch in a bike or bus lane where drivers and riders cross paths. [A01]
Glossary: Two-way left-turn lane means a center lane drivers from both directions use only to turn left. [A02]
Glossary: Diverging diamond interchange means an interchange that swaps traffic to the opposite side for uninterrupted ramp movements. [A02]
